title: Inadequate Disclosure of Registration Data
description: Parent user may not be adequately informed about what personal data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) is being collected and shared during registration, potentially including unnecessary or excessive data collection.
assumptions: Parent user may not fully understand the scope of data being shared during registration process.

title: Unintended Consequences of Data Sharing
description: Sharing sensitive data (govt ID, password) during registration may have unintended consequences such as identity theft, account compromise, or unauthorized access to parent's information.
assumptions: Parent user may not fully understand the implications of sharing sensitive personal data.

title: Inadequate Disclosure of Data in Transit
description: Metadata about the parties (parent user and authentication service) being used to link or identify them during data transmission may expose sensitive information about the registration process.
assumptions: Data flow metadata may contain identifying information about the parties involved.

title: Data Deception in Transit
description: Data in transit may be altered or tampered with, potentially leading to deceptive or misleading information reaching the authentication service.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be protected against tampering or modification.

title: Inadequate Disclosure at Authentication Service
description: Authentication service may not adequately protect or disclose how the received registration data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) will be used, stored, or shared with third parties.
assumptions: Authentication service may not have clear privacy policies or data protection measures in place.

title: Unintended Consequences at Authentication Service
description: Authentication service may process or use the registration data in ways that have unintended consequences, such as unauthorized data sharing, profiling, or misuse of sensitive information.
assumptions: Authentication service may not have adequate controls to prevent unintended data processing.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: JWT tokens and user data transmitted between Authentication Service and Parent User may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially exposing sensitive authentication credentials and personal information.

title: Information Overload at Destination
description: Parent User may receive more data than necessary for their intended purpose, including potentially unnecessary JWT tokens and user data that could be misused or cause information overload.

title: Inadequate Data Protection at Source
description: Authentication Service may not implement sufficient encryption or access controls when preparing JWT and user data for transmission, increasing risk of exposure before data leaves the system.

title: Insufficient Data Protection at Destination
description: Parent User may not adequately protect received JWT and user data, potentially leading to unauthorized access, misuse, or leakage of sensitive authentication credentials and personal information.

title: Child User lacks control over data sharing
description: Child users may not have adequate control or understanding of what personal data (parent email, password) they are sharing during login, potentially leading to unintended data disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes children may not fully understand privacy implications of login data sharing.

title: Unintended consequences from child data sharing
description: Children may not understand the implications of sharing parent email and password, potentially leading to unintended data exposure or misuse of their credentials.
assumptions: Assumes children may lack full comprehension of data sharing consequences.

title: Data disclosure during login transmission
description: Parent email and password transmitted during login flow may be exposed to unauthorized parties through interception or metadata analysis.
assumptions: Assumes data may be transmitted without adequate encryption or may be intercepted.

title: Authentication service vulnerability to intrusion
description: Authentication service may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, allowing attackers to intercept or manipulate login credentials.
assumptions: Assumes authentication service may have security vulnerabilities.

title: Denial of service during authentication
description: Authentication service may be vulnerable to denial of service attacks, potentially preventing legitimate child users from accessing the system.
assumptions: Assumes authentication service may be vulnerable to DoS attacks.

title: JWT token linkage risk
description: The JWT token containing child user type information could be used to link the child user to other data or identities, potentially enabling cross-referencing with other systems or databases.
assumptions: JWT tokens may contain or be associated with identifiers that can be correlated with other data sources.

title: Child profile disclosure risk
description: Sharing child profiles with the external entity may result in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal information about the child, potentially violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Child profiles contain sensitive personal information that should be protected from unauthorized access.

title: Flow metadata linkage risk
description: Metadata about the data flow (parties involved, data types) could be used to link or identify the child user, even if the actual data content is protected.
assumptions: Flow metadata may reveal information about the parties and data types being exchanged.

title: Data in transit interception risk
description: JWT tokens and child profiles transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to potential data compromise.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be adequately protected by encryption or other security measures.

title: Child user linkage risk
description: The child user may use the received JWT and profile information to link themselves to other data or identities across different systems.
assumptions: The child user may have access to other data sources that could be correlated with the received information.

title: Child user disclosure risk
description: The child user may disclose the received JWT and profile information to unauthorized parties, leading to potential privacy violations.
assumptions: The child user may not be bound by appropriate privacy controls or may lack awareness of privacy implications.

title: Parent provides identifying information for child
description: Parent user intentionally shares identifying data (name, DOB, govt ID) that enables identification of the child data subject. This is a legitimate identification act but creates privacy risk if the child is a minor.
assumptions: Parent is aware they are providing identifying information about a minor child.

title: Parent may link child profile to other data
description: Parent may be linking this child profile to other data they possess (medical records, school records, etc.) which could enable comprehensive profiling of the child.
assumptions: Parent has access to other data about the child and may combine it with this profile data.

title: Flow metadata enables linking
description: Data in transit may contain metadata (timestamps, IP addresses, session information) that can be used to link this child profile to other data flows or identify the parent-child relationship.
assumptions: Network metadata is captured and analyzed by third parties or system administrators.

title: Flow contains identifying information
description: The data flow itself contains identifying information about both the parent and child that could be used to identify data subjects during transit.
assumptions: Data is transmitted in a way that preserves identifying characteristics.

title: Child profile data may be disclosed
description: Child profile information (name, DOB, govt ID) stored in the system may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through security breaches or improper access controls.
assumptions: System has appropriate access controls and security measures in place.

title: System may link child profile to other databases
description: The child profile management system may link this profile to other databases or systems, enabling comprehensive profiling of the child across multiple data sources.
assumptions: System has integration with other data systems and may perform data linkage operations.

title: Potential non-compliance with minor data protection laws
description: Processing of child data may not comply with applicable data protection laws (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) requiring special consent and protection measures for minors.
assumptions: System may not have appropriate legal safeguards for minor data processing.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Child profile data may be intentionally shared with third parties (e.g., parents, guardians, external services) without proper authorization or consent, violating data minimization principles.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: The process may collect more child profile data than strictly necessary for the intended purpose, violating the minimality principle in data collection.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure via Metadata
description: MongoDB data store may inadvertently disclose personal data through metadata (e.g., access logs, query patterns) that could be used to link or identify individuals.

title: Data Loss or Corruption
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB may be lost, corrupted, or become inaccessible due to storage failures, backups issues, or system errors.

title: Excessive Data Retention
description: Child profile data may be retained in MongoDB longer than legally or operationally required, increasing exposure risk over time.

title: Child user shares more personal data than necessary
description: Child user may share excessive personal information (age, location, preferences) during video search, request, like, and comment activities beyond what is strictly required for the service functionality.
assumptions: Assumes child users may not fully understand what data is collected during video interactions.

title: Child user's identity linked to video preferences
description: Child user's identity may be inadvertently linked to their video search patterns, likes, and comments, creating a profile of their interests and potentially sensitive content preferences.
assumptions: Assumes child users may not be aware that their interactions are being tracked and linked to their identity.

title: Flow metadata used to link and identify child user
description: Metadata about the data flow (timing, frequency, content of video requests) could be used to link the child user to their video preferences and potentially identify them across different sessions.
assumptions: Assumes metadata about the flow is captured and potentially analyzed by the service or third parties.

title: Video service discloses child user data to third parties
description: Video Management Service may disclose child user data (search history, likes, comments) to third parties (advertisers, analytics partners) without proper consent or transparency.
assumptions: Assumes the service may have business relationships with third parties that require data sharing.

title: Video service non-compliant with child privacy regulations
description: Video Management Service may not comply with child-specific privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding data collection, storage, and processing of child user data.
assumptions: Assumes the service operates in jurisdictions with child privacy protections.

title: Identifying information in video metadata
description: Video metadata may contain identifying information such as timestamps, location data, user IDs, or device identifiers that can be used to identify individuals. The Video Management Service shares this metadata with the data store.
assumptions: Video metadata includes personal identifiers or quasi-identifiers that could be used for re-identification.

title: Data disclosure during video metadata transfer
description: Video metadata and files are transferred from the Video Management Service to MongoDB, representing a data disclosure across a system boundary. This transfer may expose personal data to the data store.
assumptions: The transfer of video data to MongoDB is intentional and by design for storage purposes.

title: Identifying information stored in MongoDB
description: The MongoDB videos collection stores video metadata that may contain identifying information. The data store retains this information in a persistent manner.
assumptions: MongoDB stores video metadata including potentially identifying fields.

title: Unauthorized access to stored child profile data
description: MongoDB childprofiles collection may be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of sensitive child search and watch history data.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB has appropriate access controls and encryption at rest

title: Metadata disclosure in data flow
description: Data in transit may contain metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them, potentially revealing child user identities through search and watch history patterns.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted without proper encryption or anonymization

title: Excessive data collection at source
description: Process P3 may collect and store more child search and watch history data than strictly required by the minimality principle, increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: Assumes data collection scope is defined by business requirements

title: Unauthorized access to child profile data
description: Stored child profile data may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB has appropriate access controls and authentication

title: Data loss or corruption of child profiles
description: Stored child search and watch history data may be lost or corrupted due to system failures, leading to inability to retrieve important user information.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB has appropriate backup and recovery mechanisms

title: Unintended personal data disclosure in video upload
description: Parent user may upload video containing unintended personal information (e.g., other people's faces, private conversations, sensitive documents) without realizing it.
assumptions: User may not be aware of all personal data contained in their video content.

title: Non-compliant data sharing with video management service
description: Parent user may share video data without proper authorization or in violation of applicable privacy policies and regulations.
assumptions: User may not fully understand or comply with privacy policies when uploading video content.

title: Identification through video metadata in transit
description: Meta-data about the parties (e.g., IP addresses, timestamps, user identifiers) embedded in the video upload flow may be used to link or identify the parent user.
assumptions: Video upload includes metadata that can be extracted and analyzed.

title: Unintended disclosure of video content by service
description: Video Management Service may disclose video content to unauthorized parties during approval/rejection process.
assumptions: Service may have inadequate access controls or may share data with third parties without proper authorization.

title: Data integrity compromise during video processing
description: Video Management Service may alter, corrupt, or tamper with video data during upload, approval, or rejection processing.
assumptions: Service may lack proper integrity controls or may have malicious actors.

title: Excessive data sharing at source
description: The Video Management Service may share more video data than necessary for the approved video stream, including metadata or related information beyond what is required for the child to view the content.
assumptions: Assumes the service may not be applying strict data minimization principles when streaming approved video content.

title: Data integrity during transmission
description: Video data in transit between the Video Management Service and the child user may be intercepted, modified, or corrupted during transmission, potentially compromising the integrity of the approved content.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow may not have adequate encryption or integrity protection mechanisms.

title: Non-compliant child data access
description: The child user's access to the streamed video may not comply with applicable child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K), particularly regarding consent, parental oversight, or data retention policies.
assumptions: Assumes the child user's access mechanism may not be fully compliant with child-specific privacy regulations.

title: Explicit disclosure of child browsing data to AI engine
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection explicitly shares child browsing data with the AI Recommendation Engine as part of the system design. This constitutes an intentional data disclosure of personal data (child browsing behavior) across a boundary.
assumptions: The data flow is designed to transfer child browsing data to the AI engine for recommendation purposes.

title: Data in transit may expose metadata about parties
description: Data in transit between the MongoDB collection and AI engine may contain metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them, potentially enabling correlation or identification of child users.
assumptions: Data transmission may include metadata that could be used to link or identify the child users.

title: AI engine may process or store child browsing data in privacy-risking ways
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may process or store the received child browsing data in ways that cause additional privacy risks, such as creating user profiles, making inferences about children, or storing data beyond what is necessary for the intended purpose.
assumptions: The AI engine will process the child browsing data for recommendation purposes, potentially creating user profiles or making inferences.

title: Unnecessary sharing of browsing data with third-party advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine shares browsing data with third-party advertisers, which may include more personal data than strictly necessary for the intended purpose. This violates the minimality principle in data sharing.
assumptions: Browsing data may contain personal identifiers or behavioral patterns that are not required for the advertising function.

title: Data in transit exposes metadata about data parties
description: Browsing data transferred in transit may contain metadata that reveals information about the data subjects (users) and their browsing patterns, potentially enabling profiling or linking across services.
assumptions: Data in transit may include headers or metadata that identify the data flow participants and their characteristics.

title: Third-party advertisers may process browsing data beyond intended scope
description: Third-party advertisers may receive browsing data and process it in ways that exceed the original sharing intent, potentially leading to broader data disclosure or unauthorized profiling.
assumptions: Advertisers may have their own data processing policies that could extend beyond the original data sharing agreement.

title: Browsing data enables cross-context user linkage
description: The sharing of browsing data with advertisers enables linking of user behavior across different contexts and services, potentially creating detailed user profiles beyond the original purpose.
assumptions: Advertisers may correlate browsing data with other data sources to build comprehensive user profiles.

title: Data in transit vulnerable to interception
description: Browsing data transferred between the AI Recommendation Engine and third-party advertisers may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be adequately secured or may traverse untrusted networks.

title: Unauthorized access to stored government ID images
description: Government ID images stored in the file system backend/uploads/ could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to identity theft, fraud, or misuse of personal identification information.
assumptions: Assumes the file system has appropriate access controls and encryption in place.

title: Excessive data sharing during authentication
description: The authentication service may be sharing more government ID data than strictly required for authentication purposes, violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: Assumes the authentication process collects and shares all necessary government ID data.

title: Metadata disclosure in data flow
description: Data in transit between authentication service and file system may contain metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them, potentially enabling profiling or tracking.
assumptions: Assumes metadata about the data flow is transmitted alongside the actual data.

title: User Identification via JWT Sharing
description: Authentication Service shares JWT tokens that contain user identification information, enabling identification of users across sessions and services.
assumptions: JWT tokens include user identifiers or can be linked to user identities

title: Potential Disclosure of Authentication Credentials
description: Authentication Service shares JWT tokens that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if sharing mechanisms are not properly secured.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted without adequate encryption or access controls

title: Linkability via JWT Flow Metadata
description: Data flow metadata about JWT transmission can be used to link user sessions across different authentication services or devices.
assumptions: Flow metadata includes source/destination identifiers that can be correlated

title: Persistent User Identification in localStorage
description: Browser localStorage stores JWT tokens that enable persistent identification of users across sessions and potentially across devices.
assumptions: localStorage tokens are not properly scoped or anonymized

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored JWT Tokens
description: JWT tokens stored in browser localStorage could be accessed by unauthorized parties through browser extensions, malware, or cross-site scripting attacks.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to malicious actors through browser vulnerabilities

title: Child History Data Linking via Flow Meta-data
description: The data flow DF17 transmits child history data that may contain meta-data (timestamps, locations, identifiers) that can be used to link this child to other data about the child or parent, potentially building unwanted profiles or revealing additional information about the child's activities and associations.
assumptions: Assumes the child history data includes any recurring identifiers or attributes that could be used for linking analysis.

title: Parent User Information Disclosure of Child History
description: The parent user (EE1) receives child history data which may contain sensitive information beyond what is appropriate for a parent to know, or may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the receipt process.
assumptions: Assumes the parent user may not have full authorization or may inadvertently share the received data with unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Child Data Sharing by Process
description: The Child Profile Management process (P3) may share child history data without proper authorization, consent, or without considering the child's privacy rights, potentially violating data subject consent requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the process may not have adequate consent mechanisms or may share data beyond what is necessary for the stated purpose.
